topic: The Rhythm of Heat: From Circles to Fourier Series

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Geometry of Oscillation
sections.content: Establish the fundamental connection between uniform circular motion and sine/cosine waves. Use a visual 'shadow' projection where a point rotating on a circle creates a perfect sine wave on a time-axis graph.
sections.example: A 'Robot Dog' walking in a circle; its shadow cast on a wall traces a perfect wave, representing the simplest harmonic oscillation.

sections.title: Fourier's Core Concept: Building Complexity
sections.content: Explain the Principle of Superposition: any periodic function can be reconstructed by summing simple sine and cosine waves of different frequencies. Introduce the 'Epicycle' visualization where rotating gears of varying sizes stack to trace a complex shape.
sections.example: Stacking three gears of different speeds to transform a simple circular motion into the complex silhouette of a cat's profile.

sections.title: Bridging to the Heat Equation
sections.content: Introduce the Heat Equation: a Partial Differential Equation (PDE) describing how temperature diffuses over time. Explain that the Heat Equation has 'natural modes' of decay, which are sine/cosine functions. Thus, solving heat flow is equivalent to decomposing the initial temperature distribution into Fourier components.
sections.example: A metal rod with a 'zig-zag' temperature distribution; as time passes, the Fourier components decay at different speeds, 'smoothing out' the rod's temperature.

sections.title: Application: Thermal Diffusion in a Ring
sections.content: Connect the linear heat equation to circular representations. By wrapping the rod into a ring (periodic boundary conditions), the Fourier series naturally emerges as the unique way to track heat flowing around the circle.
sections.example: A circular 'Smart Heating Coil' inside an oven; the heat stabilizes into a smooth gradient, mathematically described by the sum of its Fourier modes.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the logical chain: Circles produce Waves -> Waves combine into Series -> Series solve the Heat Equation -> Heat flow behaves like a symphony of decaying frequencies.
sections.example: A visualization showing a complex thermal map on a circular sensor being 'unpacked' into its individual frequency components (the Fourier spectrum).
